name: manual_f32db7
claim: Async generators are lazy — code inside them (including subscription/registration side effects like hub.subscribe()) does not run until the generator is first iterated, not at generator-creation time. Emitting/triggering an event before a consumer has actually started iterating a lazily-created generator silently drops that event rather than erroring

decisions.notes: A rewritten test created an async generator via iter_notification_sse(...) and immediately called hub.emit() before ever awaiting/iterating the generator, assuming the generator's internal hub.subscribe() call had already run. It hadn't -- no subscriber existed yet, so the emit was silently dropped, and the test would fall through to a 15s keepalive path instead of testing what it claimed to test. Fixed by starting the consumer as a background task and polling hub.subscriber_count until it's live before emitting. Caught by an independent Codex GPT-5.5 pass after 3 prior review phases missed it.
